title: Exact-Z/Q Pairwise-Coprime CRT Multiplication, Walsh-Hadamard Transposition, and Unpaid-Entropy Tape-Barrier Certificates
abstract: On November 24, 2026, OpenAI (openai/math) resolved the exact logarithmic exponent of n-bit integer multiplication on multitape Turing machines, proving matching Theta(n sqrt(log n)) upper and lower bounds by combining pairwise-coprime Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) cyclic-factor convolution and Walsh-Hadamard spectral steps with a tape-epoch unpaid-entropy transposition barrier governed by the critical paid-wire density rho < 1 - 1/sqrt(2) (Theorem 8.1). Here we formalize and operationalize the core algebraic, reduction, spectral-transposition, and cleared-integer entropy-barrier laws in an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (v4.35.0, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings) paired with a pure-stdlib zero-float verifier (TAPE-MUL-CERT-1.0). We machine-check unsigned product bit-length bounds, Euclidean division and integer square-root uniqueness, 3-square and 4-product polarization, cleared-integer Newton-Raphson reciprocal quadratic convergence, Newton isqrt monotonicity, 2/4-point Walsh-Hadamard involution and Parseval conservation, pairwise-coprime Bezout CRT uniqueness and reconstruction, row-major N x N transposition involution, the sharp cleared-integer unpaid-entropy bound 2(q-p)^2 > q^2 => 10p < 3q, inductive list-epoch unpaid-demand accumulation, logarithmic-exponent-1/2 separation, and epoch-vertex-to-step lower bounds. Our verifier replays 16/16 exact-Z/Q certificates in 0.024-0.875 ms (scaling to 2048-bit CRT products in 0.604 ms), cross-checks all engines against independent reference definitions, and rejects 54/54 live adversarial attacks.
